title: Week 35 Quiz — Comparative Government, Media Literacy, and Civic Action

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: A foundational set of rules establishing government powers, limits, and relationships.
questions.explanation: Constitution is the course term defined as: A foundational set of rules establishing government powers, limits, and relationships.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: The principle that public authority is bound by known and fairly applied law.
questions.explanation: Rule Of Law is the course term defined as: The principle that public authority is bound by known and fairly applied law.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: A system in which the executive emerges from and remains accountable to the legislature.
questions.explanation: Parliamentary System is the course term defined as: A system in which the executive emerges from and remains accountable to the legislature.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: A system with a separately elected executive serving a fixed term.
questions.explanation: Presidential System is the course term defined as: A system with a separately elected executive serving a fixed term.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: False or inaccurate information shared without necessarily intending harm.
questions.explanation: Misinformation is the course term defined as: False or inaccurate information shared without necessarily intending harm.

questions.prompt: Two democracies have similar constitutions, but one has weaker accountability and less access to reliable information. What does this comparison suggest?
choices: Constitutional text alone guarantees democratic performance.
Democratic performance depends on formal rules plus norms, institutions, participation, accountability, and information access.
questions.explanation: Formal constitutions matter, but democratic practice also depends on institutions, norms, accountability, participation, and information.

questions.prompt: A viral post cites an unfamiliar website for a dramatic political claim. What is the strongest first verification move?
choices: Share it quickly before it disappears.
Judge credibility from the page design.
Open new tabs, trace the claim to its original source, and compare independent credible reporting or records.
Count how many comments agree with it.
questions.explanation: Lateral reading and source tracing test a claim outside the page that is making it.

questions.prompt: What is a useful comparison between parliamentary and presidential systems?
choices: Which system has the better national character.
Which system uses more political vocabulary.
Whether either system can have courts.
How executives are selected and removed, how they relate to legislatures, and what checks structure authority.
questions.explanation: Comparative government focuses on institutional relationships and accountability rather than cultural stereotypes.

questions.prompt: A turnout table lists registered voters, ballots cast, and percentages. What check prevents a misleading comparison between districts?
choices: Verify the denominator and distinguish totals from percentages before interpreting turnout.
Compare only raw ballot totals regardless of district size.
Assume the largest district has the highest turnout rate.
questions.explanation: Percentages depend on denominators; raw totals and rates answer different questions.

questions.prompt: A student proposes a civic action on a local issue. Which plan is most responsible?
choices: Target whichever official is most famous even if that office lacks authority.
Identify the responsible jurisdiction, affected stakeholders, credible evidence, lawful action, tradeoffs, and a way to measure results.
Use an unverified viral claim because it creates urgency.
Avoid considering people who disagree with the proposal.
questions.explanation: Responsible civic action connects evidence to the correct authority and considers stakeholders, legality, tradeoffs, and measurable outcomes.

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: How can citizens evaluate institutions and information well enough to act responsibly?
shortResponse.exemplar: A full-credit response states a defensible answer to the essential question, uses two accurate details from the week, explains how each detail supports the claim, and acknowledges one complexity or limitation.
